CineGlobe_source: HMRC Creative Industries Expenditure Credit Manual
authoritative_source: HMRC Creative Industries Expenditure Credit Manual / BFI Guidelines
uplifts: IFTC uplift to 53% for independent films under £23.5m core expenditure
caps: None on AVEC; £15m qualifying cap on IFTC
hard_gates: BFI Cultural Test or official Co-Production
QPE_rule_summary: Qualifying core expenditure up to 80% of total core expenditure.
territoriality: Used or consumed in the UK
stacking: Cannot stack standard AVEC with IFTC on the same expenditure
treaty_relationships: UK is party to European Convention and various bilateral treaties

caps: Eligible expenditure capped at 80% of total global budget
QPE_rule_summary: Incurred in Greece / Greek tax resident vendors
territoriality: Services performed in Greece, billed by Greek residents
stacking: Can stack with Greek Tax Relief (30%) up to max 50% state aid limit

authoritative_source: Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 / Arts Department Guidelines
uplifts: None (formerly 16.5% base + 13.5% merit grant, now flat 30%)
thresholds: A$20M minimum QAPE for feature films
hard_gates: Training obligations; at least one Australian post/VFX provider used
QPE_rule_summary: Goods and services provided in Australia, use of land in Australia
territoriality: Provided in Australia / Australian resident tests
stacking: Cannot stack Location Offset with PDV Offset or Producer Offset
treaty_relationships: Various bilateral treaties (e.g., UK, Canada, NZ)

caps: None on base; ATL capped by local residence
hard_gates: Must be an eligible production corporation
QPE_rule_summary: Only BC-resident labor costs are fully qualifying; goods/services only if provided in BC
territoriality: Strict BC residency for labor; services rendered in BC
treaty_relationships: Canada is highly active in treaty co-productions, but PSTC does not require it
CineGlobe_mismatch: CineGlobe often misapplies DAVE strictly as a flat 16% on all post without isolating VFX-specific digital animation labor
required_remediation: Ensure DAVE is restricted strictly to eligible BC digital animation/VFX labor, not all post

authoritative_source: Georgia Department of Economic Development Guidelines
caps: ATL (compensation to single individual) capped at $500,000
hard_gates: Must include Georgia logo for 10% uplift
QPE_rule_summary: Incurred in GA; compensation to non-residents requires W-2/GA withholding
territoriality: Purchased from GA vendors; services performed in GA
CineGlobe_mismatch: CineGlobe missing the new $500k ATL individual compensation cap introduced in recent legislative changes
required_remediation: Implement per-individual $500k ATL cap on QPE

program_type: Cash Rebate / Tax Rebate (Corporate Tax Transfer)
uplifts: Can reach effectively 30% of eligible local spend (base is technically up to 30% of total eligible Hungarian spend)
caps: Non-Hungarian eligible spend can be added up to 25% of Hungarian eligible spend, meaning total rebate can be effectively 30% on up to 1.25x the Hungarian spend.
thresholds: No strict minimum, but culturally evaluated
hard_gates: Must pass cultural test; register with NFI
QPE_rule_summary: Direct film production costs in Hungary. Excludes P&A, distribution.
territoriality: Incurred with Hungarian taxpayers or foreign costs up to 25% of HU costs
required_remediation: Add Hungary base program and the 25% foreign spend inclusion rule

authoritative_source: Canary Islands Film Commission (ZEC/Corporate Tax Law)
rate: 54% for the first €1 million, 45% for the rest
uplifts: None (these are the uplifted Canary Island rates vs mainland Spain's 30%/25%)
caps: Maximum deduction of €36 million per feature film
thresholds: Minimum €1M eligible spend in Canary Islands
hard_gates: Must hire a local production service company; cultural certificate
QPE_rule_summary: Eligible expenditure in the Canary Islands
required_remediation: Add Canary Islands distinct tax credit (54%/45%) with €36M cap
